resume.note: REVIEW ROUND 1 BLOCKED, REPAIRED IN ROUND 2. The coverage work itself passed review: merge base 8bc4c661 measured 86.0/68.2/80.5 for climate.py/open_meteo.py/frontend.py, head 100.0/100.0/100.0, attribution exact and exclusive (per-module missed counts moved ONLY for those three, -21/-64/-16 = -101, matching the aggregate 1254->1153; zero movement across the other 50 modules), pragma no-cover 8 at both ends, all 24 budgeted metrics byte-identical, test-only diff with custom_components/ empty. The block was narrow: FIVE new checks were named for properties they did not pin and survived a production mutation. Three were identity tautologies -- the forecast and observed getters were compared against the private attributes they read, and both are initialised to the SAME module-level empty-series singleton (last_success to None), so the assertion held whatever the property body returned. One used a 500 response whose None body tripped a LATER guard, so the status check it was named for was never what rejected it. One asserted a resource was created, which happens on both branches of the fallback it was named for. Round 2 repaired all five test-side, no production edit: the getters now plant three distinct non-default objects and each check names the OTHER series; the 500 case carries the exact body the 200 case proves is accepted; the fallback now asserts an update-in-place outcome only that path produces, plus the shadowing-copy warning. Each repair is proven individually by tools/audit/w5-g5-195-coverage/mutation_probe.py -- 8 probes, 5 kills and 3 null controls, every production file md5-verified restored, exit 0. Coverage re-measured after the repairs: still 100.0/100.0/100.0, aggregate unchanged at 91.9 pct (14275 statements, 1153 missed). CORRECTED FIGURES the round-1 body got wrong, do not carry the old ones: new checks are +15 entities / +23 open_meteo / +10 frontend = 48 (round-1 body claimed +16/+32/+17 = 65; measured 1011->1026, 31->54, 8->18). The structure ratchet has 24 budgeted metrics, not 22 (structure_budgets.json keys less recorded_at; CLAUDE.md's 22 was wrong and was fixed in #572). The gate prints MODE FULL at this head, not the round-1 body's MODE SCOPED 3 scripts -- closures-autofix touched tests/closures.json, which makes every closure suspect; stress.py is not implicated and the change is test-only, so CI is the authority. SCOPE IS NOT tranche 1 of 3: per #505 this is tranche 1 of AT LEAST 4 and the partition is known-incomplete. Nine below-bar modules belong to no tranche, five are newer than the judge's measurement, and price_model.py, pv.py and optimizer.py have crossed below the bar since. W5-G7 MUST LEAVE #195 OPEN rather than closing it on the strength of G5 + G6 and itself; a re-partitioned tranche against #505's 30-of-53 list is still owed. process_worker.py RE-MEASURED at this head: 86.0 pct (50 statements, 7 missed) -- #505's 0.0 pct / 36-of-36 is superseded by #540, and the module also grew from 36 to 50 statements, so carry neither old number. The structural half of #505 stands regardless: there is no per-module coverage floor, only the aggregate bar, so a module can still enter the tree untested and the gate cannot see it. head_sha is the commit carrying the five repairs; the roster record commit is the one immediately after it, so the branch head is one ahead by construction. Next seat W5-G6 after this merges.

TRACK ASSERTION DENSITY, NOT PERCENTAGE, AND PROVE IT PER CHECK: this group's round-1 review blocked on five checks that reached the lines, raised the percentage and pinned nothing. A getter compared against the private attribute it reads is a tautology when both sides initialise to one shared singleton; a rejection fixture whose body a later guard rejects anyway never exercises the guard it is named for; an assertion on an outcome that occurs on both branches distinguishes neither. Give every check a fixture that discriminates, then mutate the production line the check is named for and show that check fail, plus a null control it must ignore. See tools/audit/w5-g5-195-coverage/mutation_probe.py for the shape. Do not grow the pragma no-cover count (8 sites). Script list derived from tests/run.sh, not the frozen round-2 D10 harness. CARRIED FROM #540 (#524/#525): _shutdown_process_pool must NOT be called inline from a coroutine -- it is reaped at EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP on the executor, and the atexit backstop is left with nothing to wait for. Home Assistant's own loop-protection helper (upstream, not in this tree) compares the calling thread id against the loop's; time.sleep is protected and Popen.wait is not, but CPython's Popen._wait polls with time.sleep, which is why the detector fires. A coverage test that calls the reaper directly from async context will trip it. Also: tests/nightly_ha.py's KNOWN_BLOCKING now lists two offenders this fix removed, and Checks.check BLANKS the detail on pass, so the stale pin is SILENT -- a regression of either would pass the nightly (#533).
